summary: Iteration 5 — Regression verification of the HIGH-priority publish-endpoint fix from iteration_4. The `except (*ftplib.all_errors, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:` unpacking now correctly catches the ConnectionRefusedError raised by ftplib against 127.0.0.1:1 and returns 502 with detail 'Upload failed: [Errno 111] Connection refused'. All 17 backend pytest cases pass (Projects CRUD, Preview, Components CRUD, Publish schema validation for missing host/username/unknown-protocol/unknown-project, and unreachable-host 502). Direct curl to http://localhost:8001 confirmed the JSON body and 502 status. Note: hitting the public ingress URL for this case returns Cloudflare's own HTML 502 page (Cloudflare intercepts backend-emitted 5xx responses), so the unreachable-host test now goes to localhost:8001 directly to inspect the real JSON body — this is a test-harness adjustment, not an application defect.
critical_code_review_comments: Consider adding an explicit socket.gaierror / ConnectionRefusedError branch to return a clearer message (e.g., 'Cannot reach host') instead of a raw errno string — nice-to-have, not blocking.

Cloudflare replaces backend 5xx bodies with its own HTML error page at the public ingress; the frontend PublishModal already handles this by showing a generic red toast on non-2xx, but worth documenting.

success_rate.frontend: not tested this iteration (backend-only per request)

seed_data_creation: Pytest created and cleaned TEST_it2_* and TEST_it4_pub projects plus TEST_it7_cmp components.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The unreachable-host publish test intentionally hits http://localhost:8001 directly because Cloudflare intercepts backend-emitted 5xx responses at the ingress and swaps the JSON body for its own HTML 502 page. If future changes to publish behavior need to be verified through the public URL, test only the status code and skip the JSON body assertion (or keep the localhost route as-is).
rca_of_the_issue: Fix verified: `except (*ftplib.all_errors, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:` unpacks ftplib.all_errors into a flat tuple of exception classes, so the interpreter no longer raises TypeError when evaluating the except clause. ConnectionRefusedError is a subclass of OSError and is now caught, producing the intended 502 with 'Upload failed: ...' detail.
